comments.author: David Arnoux
comments.comment:
What's the most expensive part of an agentic AI stack? It's not the models.

Most of the runtime cost is in the control logic—orchestration, state management, and error handling. The LLM API calls are often the smaller piece.

At scale, a poorly designed agent loop can cost 10x more than a simple prompt chain.
The key is to keep the agent's decision path short and deterministic where possible.

What's one design pattern you use to keep your agent costs predictable?

#AIEngineering #Agents #CostOptimization

comments.author: Avi Chawla
comments.comment:
How many of these architectures have you actually seen deployed in a production agent?

At the big tech company, I've shipped systems using four of these eight. The real gap isn't understanding the acronyms; it's knowing which one to build next.

For agentic AI, LAMs and VLMs are becoming non-negotiable. But most teams still start with an LLM and a basic RAG pipeline because it's the fastest path to a working system.

What's one architecture from this list you're actively trying to get into production?
